title: [YouPass Collect] - Water-filter Assembly
prompt: The diagram below shows how a simple water filter is constructed and how it functions to produce clean drinking water. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The diagram illustrates the structure and operation of a basic water filtration system used to produce clean drinking water.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, the process involves two main containers: a filtration drum containing three natural filtering layers and a storage drum for collecting purified water. The entire system relies on gravity to move water through the filtering materials without requiring any electrical power.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the filtration stage, untreated water is first poured into the above storage drum through an opening in the plastic lid. The drum, made of a plastic barrel, contains three distinct filtering layers arranged from top to bottom: sand, charcoal, and gravel. As water passes through these layers, impurities are progressively removed, with sand trapping larger particles, charcoal absorbing chemicals and odors, and gravel filtering out remaining sediments.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: Once the water has been filtered, it exits through a pipe connected to the upper section of the filtration drum. The filtered water then flows into the storage drum, which is positioned beside the first container and serves as a reservoir for the purified water. This drum is also sealed with a plastic lid to prevent contamination. Finally, clean drinking water can be obtained by opening a tap located at the bottom of the storage drum, allowing users to collect the filtered water for daily consumption.
